pitch:
# A kanban board for a small team

## 1. People and their journey
**Team member** (the only role). Needs to see what work exists, its stage, and who owns it; decides what to start, hand over or finish; moves cards to show progress.
Path: open the board → scan columns → create or open a card → edit, assign, move it → see the board reflect the change.

## 2. How it looks
A kanban board: a full-width page of tall vertical columns side by side, each holding a stack of white cards, like Trello-style boards.

- **Page backdrop**: fills the whole browser window, flat medium blue (#0079BF); nothing else sits behind the board.
- **Top bar**: thin strip across the top, flat darker blue (#026AA7), white text with the board name on the left and the signed-in member's initials circle on the right.
- **Column area**: below the top bar; columns sit left to right and scroll sideways when they overflow.
- **Column**: flat light grey (#EBECF0) rounded panel, 272px wide. While a card is dragged over it, it darkens to #DFE1E6.
- **Column header**: top of the column; bold dark-grey title and a small grey card count. Turns into a text box while renamed.
- **Card**: white, raised with a faint shadow, rounded, showing title and assignee initials circles. Hover: shadow deepens. Dragged: tilts slightly with a stronger shadow.
- **Card placeholder**: a flat grey (#C1C7D0) empty slot where the dragged card will land.
- **Assignee circle**: small round chip at the card's bottom right; each member has a fixed colour: red, orange, green, purple, teal, pink, in order of joining. It shows two-letter initials in white.
- **Unassigned mark**: a dashed grey outline circle on the card.
- **Add-card button**: bottom of each column, flat grey text "+ Add a card"; hover darkens the background. Pressed it becomes a title box with a blue "Add" button and a grey "×".
- **Add-column panel**: after the last column, translucent white tile "+ Add another column"; pressed becomes a name box with "Add" and "×".
- **Card dialog**: centred white panel over a 50% black dim layer, with title box, description box, assignee list with checkboxes, column name, and "Delete card" in red text. Closed by "×", Escape or clicking the dim layer.
- **Delete confirmation**: small white dialog, with a red "Delete" button and a grey "Cancel" button.
- **Refusal message**: a thin red line under the box that caused it.

## 3. How it is used
- Click "+ Add a card", type a title, press Enter or "Add": the card appears at the column bottom.
- Click a card: the card dialog opens.
- Edit title or description in the dialog: changes save when the box loses focus.
- Tick or untick a member in the dialog: assigns or unassigns them.
- Drag a card (mouse, or touch after a short hold) to any column position: it moves and the slot shows where it lands.
- Drag a column header sideways: the column is reordered.
- Click a column title: rename it; Enter saves, Escape cancels.
- Click "+ Add another column", name it, press Enter: a column is appended at the right.
- Open the column's "⋯" menu (click, or long press) and choose "Delete column": confirmation appears first.
- In the card dialog click "Delete card": confirmation appears first.
- Escape while typing in an add box: closes it, discarding the text.

## 4. Scope
One loop: view the single team board, create columns, add cards, describe and assign them, move them across columns as work progresses, and remove what is no longer needed. Customer access, billing, reports and integrations are out.

## 5. Things and their states
- **Board**: name, ordered columns. One per team.
- **Column**: name, position, ordered cards. States: normal, being renamed, being dragged.
- **Card**: title, description (may be empty), assignees, column, position. States: resting, being dragged, open in dialog.
- **Member**: name, initials, colour. Active only.

## 6. Rules
- Card title is required, 1–120 characters; empty is refused and the card is not created.
- Column name is required, 1–40 characters; empty is refused and the old name is kept.
- Description is up to 5,000 characters; excess is refused.
- A card lives in exactly one column.
- A card may have zero or many assignees; each member is assigned at most once.
- Dropping a card outside any column returns it to its original place.
- Moving a card changes only its column and position; other cards keep their order.
- Deleting a non-empty column asks for confirmation and states the number of cards that will be deleted.
- The last remaining column cannot be deleted; the action is ignored.
- Column names need not be unique.
- Deleted cards and columns are gone permanently.
- Any team member may edit any card or column.

entities_block: - **Board** (created by audience): [id: string, name: string, columns: list of Column {id: string, name: string, position: int, cards: list of Card {id: string, title: string, description: string, position: int}}, members: list of Member {id: string, name: string, initials: string, colour: string, is_active: boolean}]
action_protocol_block:
The rules the product enforces (plan the audience's side of them; the business's own back-office handling is out of view):
- [Card title required and bounded] (Board): Given a column on the board When a member submits a card with an empty title Then the card is refused and not created; When a title of 1–120 characters is submitted Then the card is created at the column bottom; When a title longer than 120 characters is submitted Then it is refused.
- [Card created at column bottom] (Board): Given a column with existing cards When a valid card is added to it Then the new card is placed at the last position of that column and other cards keep their order.
- [Column name required and bounded] (Board): Given an existing column named 'Doing' When a member renames it to an empty string Then the rename is refused and the name stays 'Doing'; When a name of 1–40 characters is given Then the rename succeeds; When a name longer than 40 characters is given Then it is refused and the old name is kept.
- [Column creation appends at right] (Board): Given a board with N columns When a member adds a column with a valid name Then it becomes column N+1 at the right end.
- [Column names need not be unique] (Board): Given a column named 'Done' exists When a member adds another column named 'Done' Then the column is created and both coexist.
- [Description length limit] (Board): Given a card When a member saves a description of 5,000 characters or fewer Then it is saved; When a description over 5,000 characters is saved Then it is refused and the previous description is kept.
- [Description may be empty] (Board): Given a card When a member clears its description Then the card saves with an empty description.
- [Card title edit validation] (Board): Given a card titled 'Draft' When a member edits the title to empty Then the change is refused and the title stays 'Draft'; When edited to a 1–120 character title Then the change saves.
- [Card lives in exactly one column] (Board): Given a card in column A When the card is moved to column B Then it is no longer in column A and is in column B only.
- [Card moves change only column and position] (Board): Given cards A, B, C in column 1 When card B is moved to column 2 at position 1 Then B's column and position change, and A and C keep their relative order and positions.
- [Drop outside any column reverts move] (Board): Given a card in column A at position 2 When it is dropped outside every column Then it returns to column A at position 2 and nothing else changes.
- [Zero or many assignees, each at most once] (Board): Given a card with no assignees When a member assigns Ana, then assigns Ana again Then the card has exactly one Ana assignment; When Ana is unassigned Then the card has no Ana assignment.
- [Last column cannot be deleted] (Board): Given a board with exactly one column When a member deletes that column Then the action is ignored and the column remains.
- [Deleting non-empty column requires confirmation] (Board): Given a column with 3 cards and at least one other column When a member chooses Delete column Then a confirmation states 3 cards will be deleted; When confirmed Then the column and its 3 cards are removed; When cancelled Then nothing is removed.
- [Deleted items are permanent] (Board): Given a deleted card When a member looks for it on the board Then it is not present and cannot be recovered.
- [Any member may edit any card or column] (Board): Given cards created by member A When active member B edits one of them Then the edit is accepted.
- [Only active members may act] (Board): Given an inactive member When a card is assigned to them Then the assignment is refused.
- [Member colour by join order] (Board): Given six members joined in order When each is shown Then their colours are red, orange, green, purple, teal, pink in that order.
- [Board presents columns left to right with card stacks] (Board): Given a board with columns in positions 1..N When the board is viewed Then columns appear left to right by position with cards stacked in order.
- [Column header shows card count] (Board): Given a column with 4 cards When the board is viewed Then the header shows the title and 4.
- [Column reorder by dragging header] (Board): Given columns A, B, C When column A is dragged to after C Then the order becomes B, C, A with positions updated.
- [Escape cancels add boxes and renames] (Board): Given an add-card box with typed text When Escape is pressed Then the box closes and the text is discarded; When renaming a column and Escape is pressed Then the old name is kept.
intent_block:
- Product type: internal_tool
- Audience: members of a small team tracking their shared work
- Goal: Let the team see what work exists, what stage each item is in, and who is doing it, by moving cards across columns on a board.
- Scope: A single kanban board per team, made of ordered columns containing cards that team members create, edit, assign, and move between columns.
- The model must cover: boards and their ordered columns (workflow stages); cards representing work items, with title and description; team members and card assignment; card position and movement between columns
- Do NOT model: customer or external user access; billing or subscription management; reporting or analytics dashboards; integrations with other tools
